newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian bourse continues to rally.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian bourse continues to rally.

text.p: The Nigerian stock market maintained its rally on Wednesday, closing stronger on a sustained rise in bank shares, traders said.
The all-share index rose to 8445.44 from 8440.93 on Tuesday.

Traders said the bank shares were attracting interest because investors were angling to gain a foothold before many would have to raise their capital bases in line with the directives of financial authorities.
Guaranty Trust Bank, which held its maiden annual general meeting as a publicly quoted company, shot up 20 kobo to 5.60 naira on positive market perception.
Consistent gainer UBA, which recently announced a major restructuring, shot up by 15 kobo to 12.55 naira.
NAL Merchant Bank strengthed at 8.40 naira, up 10 kobo while Wema Bank closed two kobo firmer at 3.80 naira.
Brewer Guinness consolidated Tuesday's gains with a five kobo ascent to 7.20 naira because investors considered the price cheap, according to dealers.
But blue chips in conglomerates, foods and petroleum marketing sectors remained depressed, weighed down by large volumes still flooding the market.
Shares of Nestle on Wednesday joined those with no buyer interest due to its poor first quarter result released on Monday. It closed steady at 52.30 naira.
Lever Brothers led falling conglomerate shares at 27.50 naira, down 20 kobo. UAC was down by a similar 20 kobo at 15.70 naira.
PZ Industries lost 15 kobo at 27.80 naira while John Holt slid by 10 kobo to 9.40 naira.

Cadbury and Nigerian Bottling Company suffered a similar fate on Wednesday. Wary investors continued to shed their hoilding, causing Cadbury a 20 kobo fall to 35.40 naira and the Coca-Cola bottler 30 kobo at 53.00 naira.
Traders said falling profitability continued to dog petroleum marketers which slid further.
African Petroleum at 55.25 naira shed 25 kobo while Total at 57.80 naira, Agip at 16.80 naira and Unipetrol at 67.40 were respective 10 kobo losers.
